source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the guiding course, principle, or path that one follows or that governs things
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often carries an ordering or normative force, not merely a physical road.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
Sentence Translations (English): The Great Way is nameless, yet all under heaven know its Way.
The sage holds to his Way and does not contend with things.
One who obtains the Way is obeyed by all under heaven.
Each of the myriad things has its own Way.
Sentences: 大道無名，天下皆知其道。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to utter a designation or description; to put something into words, especially as an act of naming or stating
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This sense is the ordinary act of verbal naming or assertion, broader than philosophical 'saying'.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone wants to speak of his good qualities.
I do not dare to say it.
He stated the facts to the crowd.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to express in words; to be capable of being spoken or formulated
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In the opening aphorism, the point is verbal formulation, not the metaphysical Way itself.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
